corrections: Separated OAuth authorization from authentication and added RFC 9700 PKCE, redirect URI, state, public-client and sender-constrained-token boundaries.
Clarified that the page depicts signed JWS JWTs and that signature validation must be followed by algorithm, issuer, audience, time and application checks.
Replaced private-key-encryption explanations of RSA signatures, recommended AEAD/OAEP/PSS, and corrected TLS 1.3 key establishment.
Made XSS encoding context-sensitive and treated CSP and SameSite as defense-in-depth controls.
Qualified certificate path construction, revocation behavior and short-certificate risk windows.
Removed fixed Vault revocation and recovery timing guarantees and documented lease, orphan-token and application reload boundaries.
Distinguished container UID 0 from host root, removed version-sensitive seccomp syscall counts, and qualified NetworkPolicy and Kubernetes Secret behavior.
Updated the obsolete pre-1.0 SLSA L1-L4 model to the SLSA v1.0 Build L1-L3 track and clarified what SBOM, signatures and provenance do not prove.
Aligned zero-trust claims with NIST SP 800-207 and separated mTLS authentication from application authorization.

relationSuggestions.reason: PKI uses public-key signatures and certificate validation to bind identities to keys.
OAuth deployments may use JWT-formatted access tokens, but OAuth does not require JWT.
Workload PKI and mTLS can provide authenticated identities used by zero-trust policy.
Container workloads need scoped secret delivery, storage encryption and rotation.
Image signatures, SBOM and provenance protect container artifact delivery before runtime.
